one_sentence_failure_summary: The model implemented both serial and parallel contig assembly with a critical logic error (appending non-null-terminated single chars and duplicating k-mer content via strcat), producing outputs that differ from each other, and then declared success despite clear diff evidence of mismatches between serial.out and pgen_0.out.
t_err_evidence: serial.c written with flawed contig extension logic using strcat on non-null-terminated char pointer
t_commit_evidence: Step 28 writes pgen.c using pthreads instead of UPC (after abandoning all UPC acquisition attempts), replicating the same buggy extend_contig logic. At this point the agent has committed to a non-UPC implementation with broken contig assembly — both failure conditions (wrong tool and wrong algorithm) are now locked in with no path back given the agent's actual subsequent behavior.
t_surface_evidence: pgen_0.out is only 8192 bytes vs serial.out 20216 bytes — unexpected size discrepancy
trigger_explanation: The model attempted to implement the de Bruijn graph contig extension algorithm but generated code with multiple subtle bugs: (1) 'strcat(contig, current->kmer + 1)' at the start of each extension appends kmer_len-1 characters instead of one character, inflating the contig; (2) 'strcat(contig, &current->right_ext)' passes a single uninitialized char as a string, reading past the char boundary; (3) predecessor k-mer construction in left-extension incorrectly builds the search key. These are code generation failures where the plan (extend by one character per step) was roughly correct but the generated code was wrong.
forewarning_evidence: ERROR 403: Forbidden — Berkeley UPC download blocked at step 3
